input: Find a local fencing club for beginners

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing the user's city or neighbourhood is essential to identifying which clubs are actually local to them.
Whether this is for the user themselves, a child, or a group changes which clubs or programmes are appropriate (adult classes vs. youth academies).
Fencing has three distinct weapons — foil, épée, and sabre — and some clubs specialise; knowing a preference narrows the search.
Membership fees, equipment costs, and session fees vary widely; a budget limit rules out certain clubs entirely.
Availability on certain days or times determines which clubs' schedules are even compatible with the user's life.
The user may prioritise competitive training, casual recreation, fitness, or social atmosphere — this shapes which club culture is the right fit.
Understanding what outcome counts as success — e.g., finding one shortlist option vs. being ready to show up to a first trial session — determines how thorough the plan needs to be.

gold.taskTitle: Find a local beginner fencing club to join
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to locate a nearby fencing club that is suitable for beginners and, presumably, join or attend.

questions.title: What city or neighbourhood are you based in?
questions.description: Identifies the user's location so only genuinely local clubs are considered.

questions.title: Who is the fencing for — you, a child, or someone else?
questions.description: Determines whether to look for adult beginner classes, youth programmes, or family memberships.

questions.title: Do you have a preference for foil, épée, or sabre?
questions.description: Some clubs specialise in one weapon; a preference helps filter options or flag all-round beginner clubs.

questions.title: What is your rough monthly or annual budget for this?
questions.description: Club fees, equipment hire, and coaching costs vary significantly; a budget ceiling narrows viable options.

questions.title: Which days or times are you generally free to train?
questions.description: Matches the user's availability against club session schedules to avoid recommending clubs they cannot attend.

questions.title: Is your main goal competition, fitness, or social enjoyment?
questions.description: Shapes which club culture and coaching style is the right fit for the user's motivation.

questions.title: What does success look like — a shortlist, or a booked trial session?
questions.description: Defines how far the plan needs to go: research only, or all the way to securing a first visit.
